Name: About this example
Note: Example data about a public plan: the planned container terminal in the southern harbour site in Helsingborg. All figures come from public sources retrieved 2026-11-17 (see each item's note and docs/v2.4.0-helsingborg-sources.md). The map is OpenStreetMap data (ODbL).

Name: Orientation decision and pre-agreement with Kemira
Note: On 21 April 2026 the municipal council took an orientation decision and a pre-agreement with Kemira AB on land; the southern city plan was adopted the same day. Source: helsingborg.se news, April 2026 (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Public consultation on the new terminal
Note: The consultation ran 23 September to 6 November 2026 and is concluded; a consultation report is being prepared and becomes part of the environmental permit application. Source: port.helsingborg.se/om-hamnen/ny-containerhamn/ (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Detailed planning and engineering
Actor: City of Helsingborg, Port of Helsingborg
Note: Engineering started after the decision of 21 April 2026 and detailed plans are being drawn up. Sources: helsingborg.se April 2026; port.helsingborg.se (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Environmental permit application
Actor: Port of Helsingborg, Land and Environment Court
Note: The application to the Land and Environment Court is planned for the end of 2027; the process is expected to take at least two years and permits could be in place around 2030. Source: port.helsingborg.se/om-hamnen/ny-containerhamn/ (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: New quay, about 650 m at 15 m depth
Quay depth: 15 m (new quay); 13 m in West Harbour today
Vessel class: 3 feeders or 2 Post-Panamax in a row; today vessels up to 225 m, new quay about 300 m
Note: A new quay with 15 metres of water depth is planned, about 650 metres long, with room for three or two really large vessels in a row. In West Harbour today: 13 metres depth and vessels up to 225 m. Sources: port.helsingborg.se (sv and en), helsingborg.se April 2026 (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Dredging and water works
Quay depth: seabed dredged to at least 9 m
Actor: Port of Helsingborg, Swedish Transport Administration
Note: The seabed is to be dredged to at least nine metres; sediment dispersal has been modelled (consultation material, dredging and dumping appendices 2025); the fairway is widened per the Swedish Transport Administration's decision basis SSY2602. Dredging contaminated sediments is also a remediation measure. Sources: helsingborg.se April 2026; port.helsingborg.se consultation material; bransch.trafikverket.se (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Cranes and the aRTG system
Vessel class: STS cranes up to 80 m high; RTG cranes 21–24 m, five container tiers
Note: The new handling system consists of electric RTG cranes over the container yard blocks, making the port nearly fossil-free and automated. Along the new quay, 6 STS cranes are drawn in the city's and the port's published vision renders (the count read from the images; consistent with berth math: 650 m corresponds to about three berths of two cranes each). In West Harbour today there are three large STS cranes (quay 904). Sources: port.helsingborg.se; helsingborg.se vision image April 2026; port.helsingborg.se news 2025-09-19 (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: New combi terminal and rail link
Actor: Port of Helsingborg, City of Helsingborg, Swedish Transport Administration
Note: A new combi terminal is built next to the new container terminal, linking sea and rail. The city is also investigating a southern harbour track from the freight yard (a separate project); a connecting track to the combi terminal was planned at about SEK 85 million. Today the combi terminal (Interlink) at Gåsebäck handles daily trains. Sources: port.helsingborg.se/landtjanster/kombiterminal/; dagenslogistik.se (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Shore power (OPS) for container vessels
Note: The port's first shore-power facility for container vessels, the first in Scandinavia; planned start of operation autumn 2026 at the quay in West Harbour. Capacity up to 3.5 MW; reduced emissions up to 8,000 t CO2, 100 t NOx and 5 t SOx per year. With the relocation virtually the whole port is electrified, including shore power, so the technology carries over to the new terminal. Sources: port.helsingborg.se/2025/08/05/landstrom-till-containerfartygen-nasta-steg-i-hamnens-klimatomstallning/; bransch.trafikverket.se SSY2602 (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Investment
Note: A PwC report commissioned by the port, published 2025-01-28: the investment is estimated at SEK 2.6 billion with a payback of about 22 years, financed without municipal support. The port's current estimate is about SEK 3.4 billion; a final investment decision can be taken only once the permits are in place. Sources: port.helsingborg.se/en/2025/01/28/new-report-significant-benefits-of-moving-the-container-terminal-south/; port.helsingborg.se/om-hamnen/ny-containerhamn/ (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Construction time two to three years
Note: Construction can start only once the permits are in place (possibly around 2030); the build time is estimated at two to three years. Construction proceeds in parallel with today's operations in West Harbour. Source: port.helsingborg.se/om-hamnen/ny-containerhamn/ (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Name: Commissioning around 2033
Note: The new terminal is expected to enter operation around 2033 and handle more than twice as many containers per year as today (about 100,000 container trucks per year today). The Swedish page states 2033; the same English page states 'about 2030' in its body while its heading says 2033. Sources: helsingborg.se April 2026; port.helsingborg.se sv and en (retrieved 2026-11-17).
